 Runners hit malls to beat haze
 By The Star 
 Photos By Photos: AZLINA ABDULLAH/ 
 Wednesday, 11 Nov 2026

A pack 
of runners in an indoor 
running event organised by Atria Shopping Gallery in Petaling Jaya. 
 THERE were crowds of a different kind at several shopping complexes in the Klang Valley, thanks to the haze that never seemed to fully go away.
 They were not racing for the best deals, but instead grabbing the chance to exercise in a makeshift indoor arena away from smoke-filled skies.
 In Petaling Jaya, Atria Shopping Gallery organised several sessions to encourage people to stay active and maintain their fitness despite the recent hazy conditions.
 Held in collaboration with fitness studio The Active Chimp, the event titled “Run The Mall: Beat the Haze, Keep the Pace” attracted a few hundred participants of various ages.
 Participants warming up before a ‘Run the Mall’ session at the Atria shopping centre in Petaling Jaya. 
 With a coach leading warm-up sessions and a jogging circuit marked out on Level 1, the sessions gave urbanites a chance for some exercise within the air-conditioned climes of the mall.
 Meanwhile, Paradigm Mall held the inaugural “Mallathon” in partnership with Little Grappy Running Association (LGRA).
 The free, beginner-friendly indoor community session drew a highly diverse crowd of seniors, families and enthusiastic community runners.
 Indoor running helping people get some exercise while avoiding the unhealthy conditions outside. 
 In Kuala Lumpur, The Starhill hosted two sessions of “Escape the Haze” organised by the popular Worst Pace Scenario Run Club in collaboration with Upbound.
 The fast-paced, 35-minute indoor loop wound through the luxury tiers of the mall in Bukit Bintang and went rather viral.
 And if you feel like you have missed out, worry not.
 Atria Shopping Gallery has announced that it welcomes everyone to utilise the mall for exercise.
 Atria Shopping Gallery is opening up its premises for exercise daily, but asks runners to give way to shoppers. 
 It said runners could use Level 1 for exercise every day, from 10am to 10pm. However, it advises users to keep a moderate pace, with no sprinting.
 It also asked runners to always give way to shoppers, as well as to be considerate and stay safe.
